text: The ink remained wet beneath the library's colorless light. It had pooled slightly at the hooks of the letters, as if the Ledger had written in haste, though nothing else in the chamber suggested urgency. The jars stood motionless on their shelves. The tiny figures within them continued their unfinished gestures, repeating movements too small to make a sound. Even the walls had quieted. Ninsun could hear Zik's breathing beside her and, beneath it, the faint settling of the copper figurine in her fist whenever her grip shifted.

text: Zik had not moved since the sentence appeared. His left hand remained fixed to the calcified key resting against the Ledger, the distinction between his skin and the pale mineral around it nearly gone. The grayness that had begun at his fingertips now crossed the back of his hand in branching lines, climbed his wrist, and vanished beneath his sleeve. More of it showed above his collar. It followed the veins of his throat like writing worked beneath the skin by someone who had no patience for spacing.

text: The Ledger occupied most of its surface. Blank pages waited beyond the command, their edges clean despite the dust coating everything around them. The quill lay to the right, set parallel to the book's spine with the care of an instrument prepared before a procedure. Its shaft had the same chalk-white texture as the key fused to Zik's hand. No inkpot stood nearby. There were no stains on the desk, no discarded nibs, no scraped practice marks. Yet the final sentence shone as if written seconds ago.
